Specifically, only single unique pictures, regardless of type or associated track, are in memory. > - There can be more than one picture of a given type per track file except for type 1 (32x32 png icon) of which there can be only one and it needs to be png. > - Pictures of the same type are ordered and can be reordered per track file. > - Pictures that are associated/referenced by a given file, regardless of the picture’s origination (from track file or added in editor), are considered “pinned” for the UI descriptions that follow. Pictures de-pinned from tracks remove the track’s reference to a picture and do not remove a track’s association with a picture in its source file. > -

Under High-Risk Concerns you wrote “Shared pooled-image references can produce unexpected bulk changes if track association boundaries are unclear in UI, especially with bytes-only dedupe identity.” We are going to keep any meta data differences per track reference so the UI should and pool should “see” these pictures are different. Do not change the plan, just expand a bit more on why you think this an issue and perhaps some methods to diminish the concern if there still is one. You’re right that per-track-reference metadata removes one major ambiguity. I’ll explain the remaining risk as an operational/reference risk (not a metadata-collision risk), and list concrete mitigations. Good callout. With metadata stored per track-reference, that specific “same bytes but different metadata get merged incorrectly” risk is mostly addressed. The remaining risk I had in mind is this: - If multiple tracks reference the same pooled image bytes, any action that is implemented at pool-item scope instead of reference scope can still affect more tracks than intended. - Typical failure modes are remove/reorder/pin operations accidentally touching every reference to that pooled item. - UI confusion

Ok, add to the plan (editing as needed for clarity and brevity) your suggestions on how to diminish concern without changing plan scope, especially the tests. And a potential todo to the plan that calls for updating the UI to include picture meta data information. Currently de-pinning a picture removes it from the list - not desired. I think I made a mistake in my wording used in initial design work. Pinning and reference making are not exactly the same thing. The desired result is that a user can browse any of the pictures based on type and then “pin” the picture(s) that they would like to be saved to a given track (selected or all). De-pinning a picture should not remove the picture from the available list of pictures it just means don’t save that picture to the track’s file.
